title.narrative: Area-Based Response in North Darfur: Addressing WASH and Food Security Needs Amid Protracted Crisis

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtAmid the crisis initiated in April 2023, North Darfur has become one of the most severely affected regions ranking as the 3rd state of origin for IDPs and the 2nd largest host state for displaced populations. In El Fasher alone, 54% of displaced individuals remain within the locality, while 15% have moved to Tawila and 14% to Dar As Salam – DMT Sudan, 20.12.24. In El Fasher, famine and food insecurity persist, notably in IDP camps such as Zamzam, Abu Shouk, and Al Salam. Tawila has shifted from IPC Phase 3 to Phase 4 (Emergency) due to a rapid influx of IDPs, with 5% of households now in IPC Phase 5 (Catastrophe). The FRC warns of a high famine risk in Tawila for the December 2024/May 2025 period. Skyrocketing food prices have forced many households to skip meals, rely on wild foods, or resort to begging, while agricultural livelihoods have been severely impacted due to insecurity, land degradation, and a lack of access to seeds and tools. ltbrgtIn response, Solidarités International (SI) and Dar for Community Development (DCD), aim to provide lifesaving and life-sustaining support to people affected by the crisis. The intervention will target IDPs, returnees and host communities’ households in Tawila, Saraf Omra, and El Fasher, addressing both water and food security needs. This response is designed to improve living conditions and enhance food security, directly benefiting 62,680 individuals, including 16,296 men, 19,430 women, 11,910 boys, and 15,044 girls from the affected areas. ltbrgtSI will provide life-sustaining livelihood support to 3,180 households across Tawila and Saraf Omra to enhance food security and resilience. The intervention includes distributing drought-resistant cereal seeds and farming tools tailored to local preferences to 2,650 farmers, along with home gardening kits for 530 households lacking land access. ltbrgtTo ensure sustainable impact, SI will organize farmers into 127 farmers groups, each led by trained lead farmers who will disseminate best practices in agriculture, post-harvest handling, and nutrition. Training will be conducted in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture, with demonstration plots established for vegetable gardeners. ltbrgt ltbrgtDCD will implement WASH interventions to address the urgent water needs within El Fasher town and Zamzam IDP Camp. The response includes a 30-day emergency water trucking operation, delivering 139.5 cubic meters of safe drinking water daily to a total of 18,600 individuals across Zamzam Camp and IDPs gathering points in El Fasher. Water quality monitoring will complete the water trucking activities to guarantee the consistent provision of safe, potable water. DCD will rehabilitate five water stations and support the ongoing operation and maintenance of the 4 of them by training four water user committees. These committees will be equipped with the necessary tool kits and skills to manage water resources effectively. Moreover, DCD will ensure the operation and maintenance of 5 additional Water Yards. These efforts aim to reduce waterborne diseases, improve health outcomes, and strengthen the community's ability to sustainably manage its water resources, contributing to the overarching goal of improving the well-being and resilience of the impacted population. ltbrgtBy providing both WASH and Food Security and Livelihoods activities, this response will address the immediate needs of the targeted households, while allowing them to recover from the shock. The proposed intervention will contribute to improving food security, safeguarding livelihoods, and reducing morbidity and mortality related to inadequate access to water and food in the context of the ongoing crisis in North Darfurltbrgtlt/pgt
